as_told.title: Elongated skulls appear suddenly in Amarna-period art

plain: A researcher named Luke Caverns, on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2025, tells how an ancient Egyptian king, Amenhotep IV, took the throne after his father died and declared he would no longer worship Amun, the god the great Karnak temple was built for. Caverns says the king shut Karnak's doors, turned only to the sun god called the Aten, renamed himself Akhenaten, and fell out with the priests. He adds that Egyptian art then changed suddenly, showing royals with long, stretched skulls, and says nobody knows where that came from or why it appeared just then, which to him hints at an unexplained outside influence.
